subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` be a hard-enforced Telegram DM security boundary, and if so should enforcement use a shared direct-aware tool-policy resolver?
rationale: The schema and types already advertise a security-sensitive DM policy surface, but current runtime enforcement does not read that direct config; choosing enforcement, retirement, or deferral changes operator security expectations and config compatibility.

options.title: Enforce Direct DM Policy
options.body: Treat the existing direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with precedence and isolation tests.

options.title: Retire The Accepted Surface
options.body: If DM-level hard enforcement is not intended, reject or migrate the config and document the supported alternative so operators do not rely on a silent no-op.

options.title: Defer To Binding Policy Design
options.body: Keep this open behind the broader policy design, accepting that Telegram direct policy remains unreliable until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct DM Policy
recommendation.body: Treat the existing direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with precedence and isolation tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans config compatibility, Telegram channel behavior, and runtime security posture where recent history points to this owner as the best routing candidate.
